prompt: What does each line of `cases/dev.jsonl` hold?

choices.text: A prompt and the score it reached on the set
choices.why: Scores are computed from runs.

choices.text: A message and its token count under the model
choices.why: Token counts are in the run files.

choices.text: A message and the label that a person gave it
choices.why: Right: the input and the judgement.

choices.text: A message and the reply the model gave to it
choices.why: Replies are in the run files, not the cases.

prompt: Why write each label before running the prompt on the message?

choices.text: So the label is a judgement of the message itself
choices.why: Right: after the reply, you are judging the reply instead.

choices.text: Because the harness refuses unlabelled cases
choices.why: It would, but that is not the reason.

choices.text: Because running first changes the model's weights
choices.why: Running changes nothing in the model.

choices.text: So the label can be copied from the model's own reply
choices.why: That is the mistake the rule prevents.

prompt: `v2` against `v3` gave p = 0.070, and `v4` against `v3` gave p = 0.021. What separates the two results?

choices.text: The prompts were run on two different machines
choices.why: They were run one after the other.

choices.text: Only the second one used a holdout set
choices.why: Both were on dev.

choices.text: The first comparison ran at a higher temperature
choices.why: All three ran at 0.

choices.text: Two messages in the count of those that changed
choices.why: Right: eight changed against ten, on either side of 0.05.

prompt: A set of 40 cases sees differences of about ten points. Roughly how many cases would it take to see differences half that size?
Put `pl check`'s checks in the order they run.
Which checks could run on every reply in production, where no person has labelled the message?

choices.text: `category` and `urgency`, with the model as the label
choices.why: They need a person's label.

choices.text: `json`, `fields` and `labels`, which read only the reply
choices.why: Right: they need only the reply and the contract.

choices.text: All five, run against yesterday's labels
choices.why: Yesterday's labels belong to yesterday's messages.

choices.text: None of them, since all five need a test set
choices.why: Three need only the reply.

prompt: `t37` failed `json`. Why is it not also listed as a wrong category?

choices.text: The `category` check skips any message ending in a question
choices.why: No check reads the message's punctuation.

choices.text: The harness lists only one failure per run file
choices.why: It lists one per reply.

choices.text: A reply that fails one check is not scored on the next
choices.why: Right: there is no category in a reply nobody can read.

choices.text: Its category happened to be right
choices.why: Nothing read its category.

prompt: Which of these make a check worth having, according to the section? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: It gives the same verdict every time
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: It asserts one property
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: It is as strict as whatever reads the reply
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: It is written by a model rather than a person
choices.why: A check that can change its mind is a second thing to measure.

prompt: Why does `v3-examples.txt` pass 28 of 40 on `dev.jsonl` and only 14 of 30 on `holdout.jsonl`?
hint: Who wrote each set, and when?

choices.text: Dev was written with the prompt, the holdout after
choices.why: Right: the author imagined the easier messages.

choices.text: The holdout runs at a higher temperature by default
choices.why: Both ran at 0.

choices.text: The model has seen the dev messages during training
choices.why: The course wrote them; nothing suggests that.

choices.text: The holdout's labels are wrong
choices.why: They were written the same way, by a person.

prompt: `v3` beat `v4` on dev by 28 to 20, and on the holdout by 14 to 4. What does that say?

choices.text: The holdout is easier than dev
choices.why: Both prompts scored lower on it.

choices.text: The holdout must now be used to tune the examples
choices.why: Tuning on it would make it a second dev set.

choices.text: The examples' gain was fitted to dev
choices.why: It held, and grew, on messages it was not chosen on.

choices.text: The choice held on messages it was not made on
choices.why: Right: the other half of a holdout's job.

prompt: A second set, built apart and run only when deciding, so that it is never tuned against, is called a ___ set.
After shipping, you read why `h01` fails, change the prompt until it passes, and report the new holdout score. What is wrong with that?

choices.text: Nothing, since the holdout score went up
choices.why: It went up on a case you tuned against.

choices.text: `h01` has become a dev case, tuned against
choices.why: Right: and the holdout needs replacing.

choices.text: The holdout must be run at temperature 1 after a change
choices.why: Temperature is not the issue.

choices.text: Holdout cases may not be read by a person at all
choices.why: Reading is fine; tuning to them is the problem.

prompt: `v11-contaminated.txt` uses `t22`, `t25` and `t26` as its examples. What happens to those three cases?

choices.text: Their labels change to whatever the example says
choices.why: The labels are in the case file and do not move.

choices.text: They become harder for the model to answer
choices.why: They become trivial.

choices.text: They pass their category, by copying
choices.why: Right: they can no longer fail it.

choices.text: They are dropped from the run by `pl run`
choices.why: `pl` runs every case in the file.

prompt: On the 37 dev messages that are not its examples, how many does `v11-contaminated.txt` pass?
Contamination left the dev total at 28 and took the category count from 35 to 39. Why is that the dangerous shape?

choices.text: It reads as progress in one line of the table
choices.why: Right: a better category count after somebody improved the examples.

choices.text: Because 39 of 40 is above the 0.05 threshold
choices.why: That threshold is for a sign test, not a count.

choices.text: Because the holdout is never run after it
choices.why: It was, and it fell from 14 to 9.

choices.text: Because the total exposes it at once
choices.why: The total did not move at all.

prompt: Two runs of the same prompt at temperature 1, with different seeds, passed 27 and 28. How many messages changed result between them?
At temperature 1, `t36` failed all five calls, and it passes at temperature 0. What kind of finding is that?

choices.text: Noise that five samples are too few to see
choices.why: Five of five is not noise.

choices.text: A stable defect in the prompt, found by one run
choices.why: At temperature 0 it passes.

choices.text: A wrong label, since it fails so consistently
choices.why: The same label passes at temperature 0.

choices.text: The setting is part of what is being tested
choices.why: Right: the prompt and its temperature are one thing.

prompt: A test that passes and fails the same input on different calls is called ___.
Match each observation from this lesson to what it tells you.

pairs.left: `t25` fails five of five, and at temperature 0
pairs.right: A stable disagreement one run finds

pairs.left: `t07` fails five of five, as `high` and as `low`
pairs.right: No settled answer, under a stable count

pairs.left: 39 categories of 40 with three copied examples

prompt: A colleague reports: "New prompt: 30/40 on dev, up from 28. Ship it." The prompt runs at temperature 0.7 and was tuned on dev. What do you ask for?

choices.text: Nothing more: two cases up is enough to ship
choices.why: Two cases from one sampled run is noise-sized.

choices.text: Rates over samples and a holdout run
choices.why: Right: and the cases that changed.

choices.text: A run at temperature 1.0 to confirm the gain
choices.why: A hotter run measures something else.

choices.text: A larger dev set built from the new prompt's replies
choices.why: Labels must come before replies.

prompt: Which of these is the strongest evidence that one prompt is better than another?

choices.text: Two more passes on the dev set it was tuned on
choices.why: Tuned-on sets flatter.

choices.text: A higher category count with three examples from dev
choices.why: That is the contaminated table.

choices.text: Ten fixed and none broken on a holdout
choices.why: Right: messages it was not chosen on, with a lopsided split.

choices.text: A single run at temperature 1 that passed one more
choices.why: One message is what two seeds differed by.
